title: Canonical Candidate Seam
statement: Let $M_V$ be a finite machine over Boolean symbols, let $x$ and $s$ be Boolean words, and let $b$ be a Boolean phase. The buffered composition of the assembly machine with $M_V$, started from the assembly machine's configuration on input $x$ with phase $b$ and word $s$ on its work tape, equals the configuration on input $x$ whose state is the first-phase state corresponding to $b$, whose tape zero stores $s$, whose other work tapes are blank with heads at zero, whose input head is at position one, and whose output is empty.
replaced:
For any verifier machine $MV$, words $x, s$, and assembly phase: the buffered
composition's first-phase configuration over the assembly machine prepared with
candidate $s$ equals the canonical configuration in which control sits in the
chosen assembly phase, tape zero carries $s$, and all other tapes (composition
buffer and verifier work) are blank.
